title: Sakuraco Alternatives: 5 Japanese Snack & Tea Boxes - Cratejoy
summary: Looking for a Sakuraco alternative? Compare five Japanese snack and tea boxes by delivered cost and contents, from Bokksu to a seasonal pantry box.
body_markdown:
## The alternatives


Closest match to Sakuraco


### Bokksu vs Sakuraco


**Best for:** A subscriber who likes the Sakuraco format and wants a different curator’s picks.


[Bokksu](https://www.bokksu.com/) ships 20 to 22 Japanese snacks, sweets, and a tea from Japan each month, sourced from family makers and themed around the seasons. Its culture guide lists each item’s origin, flavor notes, and common allergens.


#### What feels familiar


Traditional sweets and savory snacks, a new tea each month from matcha to hojicha, and a printed guide to the theme.


#### What changes


Bokksu describes its box as snacks and tea, with no home good. Delivered to the US, a monthly box comes to about $57, a few dollars under Sakuraco. Prepaid plans add extra gift snacks.


Teas and hot-spring goods from Japan


### Onsen Box vs Sakuraco


[Monthly Onsen Box (Japanese Wellness Sets)](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/monthly-onsen-box-japanese-wellness-sets-onsenbox) by Onsen Box


From $88.60 / box


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/monthly-onsen-box-japanese-wellness-sets-onsenbox)


**Best for:** The Sakuraco fan who liked the tea and the regional finds more than the sweets.


Onsen Box is a Japan-based seller that builds each month’s set around the country’s hot-spring towns. A box can hold rare herbal teas, organic first-harvest teas, local health foods, and onsen bath additives.


#### What feels familiar


Regional teas and local specialties packed in Japan, with a mix that changes by season.


#### What changes


Wellness takes over from snacking, so expect bath goods next to the tea. At $93.60 a month, it is the priciest box on this list.


Just the tea, for less


### Simple Loose Leaf Tea vs Sakuraco


1st box


50% off


Preferred Seller


[Premium Loose Leaf Tea Discovery Subscription](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/premium-loose-leaf-tea-discovery-subscription-simplelooseleaf) by Simple Loose Leaf Tea Company


From $14.98 / box


Free shipping


[Shop Now](https://www.cratejoy.com/products/premium-loose-leaf-tea-discovery-subscription-simplelooseleaf)


**Best for:** The subscriber who stayed for the tea pairing and can do without the snacks.


Simple Loose Leaf Tea Company sends two to four pouches of loose-leaf tea a month, each good for about 12 cups, with tasting notes and steeping instructions. You fill out a tea profile or choose a green-tea-only plan, and the green teas on its list include sencha and genmaicha.


#### What feels familiar


A monthly tea you didn’t choose, with instructions for brewing it well.


#### What changes


There are no snacks, and the teas come from US tea companies and small farms across Asia. Two pouches cost $15.94 a month with free shipping, less than Sakuraco charges for shipping alone.


A seasonal Japanese pantry


### Kokoro Care vs Sakuraco


**Best for:** A cook who wants Japan’s regional pantry foods along with its sweets, and would rather pay four times a year.


[Kokoro Care](https://kokorocares.com/products/seasonal-subscription-package) ships a package of seasonal foods from Japan every three months, each item made by a local farmer or small-batch producer. The fall 2026 box has houjicha yokan, miso candied sweet potato, smoked daikon pickles, a smoked tofu bar, and five-grain udon, with an English brochure of producer stories and recipes.


#### What feels familiar


Small Japanese makers, regional specialties, and a box that follows the season.


#### What changes


It arrives quarterly and leans toward pantry foods you cook with. The $85 subscription price includes shipping and import duties to the US and Canada, which works out to less than $30 a month. You can also buy a single package for $95.


Modern snacks instead of wagashi


### TokyoTreat vs Sakuraco


**Best for:** Someone who would trade wagashi and senbei for seasonal Kit Kats and a bowl of ramen.


[TokyoTreat](https://tokyotreat.com/) is Sakuraco’s sister brand and shares its prices, shipping fees, and help center. The box swaps small makers for big snack brands such as Pocky, Hi-Chew, and Calbee, plus Japan-only Kit Kat flavors, noodles, and drinks like Ramune. A 20-page booklet explains the snacks.


#### What feels familiar


A themed monthly box on the same billing, with a booklet to read while you taste.


#### What changes


The snacks turn modern and full size, and the drinks lean toward sodas over tea. The home good is gone, and the monthly cost stays the same.
